newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch travel agents condemn KLM commission cut.
newsitem.headline: Dutch travel agents condemn KLM commission cut.

text.p: The Dutch association of travel agencies said on Friday it would challenge the decision of airline KLM to reduce travel agents' commissions.
From April 1, KLM will pay travel agents a commission of 7.5 percent on ticket sales, down from the present rate of nine percent.
"The direct result of this decision is an estimated fall of 16 percent in the income for the travel agent in KLM business. This is about 20 to 30 million guilders," the ANVR said in a statement.
It said it was advising its members to reject KLM's decision.
It added it was asking KLM to reconsider its decision and agree to talks within eight days.
KLM said it had already been in talks with the travel agents for two years.
"It has not come as a complete surprise and we will not be changing our decision," a KLM spokesman said.

He added that an internal study had concluded that the the average cost plus commission for a travel agent of issuing a ticket was 85 guilders. The lower commission would still give them, on average, 105 guilders per ticket.
KLM would also continue to offer extra commissions of up to six percent, he said.
